judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY TWO Performance Objectives under the same Theme (MENSURATION AND GEOMETRY) but in distinct Sub-Themes/Topics: the first ('use meters and centimetres as standard measuring units') sits in Primary Measures > Length, while the second ('identify the use of standard measuring units', per LC for area) sits in Secondary Measures > Area. judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same Primary Three Topic '1. Symmetry' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). Objective 1 (first) is 'identify shapes with line(s) of symmetry'; Objective 2 (second) is 'identify lines of symmetry in everyday life'. Proficiency in identifying lines of symmetry within defined geometric shapes substantively supports the broader application of recognizing lines of symmetry in everyday-life objects, a meaningful extension from structured shapes to real-world contexts. This is a supported developmental direction (first_to_second) rather than mere shared wording; the shared 'symmetry/identify' tokens and same-page proximity are corroborating but not the basis. Grade rank is equal (both Primary Three), and the source objective numbering plus the shapes-to-application progression provides substantive same-rank directional evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic '2. Fractions' (Sub-Theme Fraction). The second objective ('divide shapes into ½, 1/3, ¼ etc.') develops concrete/visual fraction sense by partitioning shapes into unit fractions, which is a more foundational competency. The first objective ('write fractions which have the same value as a given fraction') requires understanding what a fraction represents in order to reason about equivalence, a conceptually more advanced skill. Proficiency in partitioning shapes into fractions plausibly supports success in writing equivalent fractions, giving a same-rank developmental direction from the second toward the first. Shared LC tag 'fractions' and source proximity corroborate topical coherence but were not used alone as the basis.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same Primary Three Topic '3. Multiplication'. The first objective, 'multiply from 1 x 1 to 9 x 9', establishes single-digit multiplication fact fluency, and the second, 'multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number', requires applying those known facts to a larger, more complex procedure. Mastery of basic multiplication facts substantively supports success in multiplying a 2-digit by 1-digit number, a genuine increase in complexity rather than mere repetition. Though both share rank 2 (Primary Three), the objective texts show a clear developmental progression from facts to multi-digit application, justifying buildsTowards from first to second. Shared hierarchy and token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient.

judgment.rationale: First objective is a general multiplication skill (multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number) under Basic Operations > Multiplication; second applies multiplication in a money context (simple multiplication involving money, product not exceeding ₦20) under Mensuration and Geometry > Primary Measures > Money. Both are Primary Three (same rank). Proficiency in the general multiplication procedure substantively supports success in applying multiplication to money problems, so the directional support runs first_to_second (foundational computation to contextual application) rather than symmetric coincidence. Shared LC tag 'multiplication' and objective wording overlap corroborate topical coherence, but the pair-specific application relationship justifies the developmental direction.
